Tips and common mistakes
Taking 20% of a gross price to find the VAT. Divide by 1.2 first.
Quoting business prices ex-VAT to consumers. UK consumer prices must include VAT.
Confusing zero-rated with exempt. They affect reclaiming differently.
Forgetting to register on time once you pass the threshold.
Checking an invoice
A valid UK VAT invoice shows the supplier's VAT registration number, the date, a description of the goods or services, the net amount, the VAT rate and the VAT charged. Use the calculator to check that net plus VAT equals the gross total. If you're VAT-registered, you need a valid invoice to reclaim input VAT, so ask the supplier for a corrected invoice when the figures don't add up.
Frequently asked questions
How do I add 20% VAT?
Multiply the net price by 1.2.
How do I remove VAT from a price?
Divide the gross price by 1 plus the rate (1.2 for 20%), then subtract to get the VAT.
What is the UK VAT rate?
20% standard, 5% reduced, 0% zero rate.
Why isn't the VAT 20% of the total?
Because the total already includes the VAT. VAT is 20% of the net price, which is 1/6 of the gross.
When do I need to register for VAT?
When taxable turnover passes the registration threshold in any rolling 12-month period, or you expect it to in the next 30 days.
Can I reclaim VAT?
VAT-registered businesses can usually reclaim VAT on business purchases. Consumers can't, except in schemes such as tourist refunds abroad.

W-4 Withholding Estimator 2026 | FigSumo (40 chars)
Meta description
Estimate federal income tax withholding per paycheck using IRS Publication 15-T percentage method for 2026. Compare with IRS Tax Withholding Estimator. (151 chars)

US

1,082 (minimum 1,000)
H1: W-4 Withholding Estimator
Form W-4 tells your employer how much federal income tax to withhold from each paycheck. If too little is withheld, you'll owe at tax time and possibly an underpayment penalty; too much, and you're giving the government an interest-free loan until your refund arrives. This calculator projects your 2026 federal income tax, compares it with what you're on track to have withheld, and suggests an extra amount per paycheck for Step 4(c) of your W-4.
How to use this calculator
1. Filing status: single, married filing jointly or head of household.
2. Pay frequency and annual wages (from all jobs; for two-earner couples, include both).
3. Pre-tax deductions: 401(k), HSA and Section 125 health premiums reduce taxable wages.
4. Other income: interest, dividends, side income not subject to withholding.
5. Deductions: itemized deductions above the standard deduction, if any.
6. Credits: for example the Child Tax Credit ($2,200 per qualifying child in 2026).
7. Federal tax withheld so far this year, paychecks remaining and withholding per paycheck (from your latest pay stub).
Results: projected 2026 tax, projected total withholding, amount you'd owe or get back, and the extra withholding per paycheck to break even.
How it works
Taxable income = Wages − Pre-tax deductions + Other income − Standard (or itemized) deduction
Projected tax = Tax from 2026 brackets − Credits
Projected withholding = Withheld to date + Per-paycheck withholding × Paychecks left
Extra per paycheck = (Projected tax − Projected withholding) ÷ Paychecks left
2026 standard deduction: $16,100 single, $32,200 married filing jointly, $24,150 head of household.
2026 single brackets: 10% to $12,400; 12% to $50,400; 22% to $105,700; 24% to $201,775; 32% to $256,225; 35% to $640,600; 37% above.
Worked examples
Example 1: single, $75,000 salary, mid-year check
Taxable income = 75,000 − 16,100 = $58,900
Projected tax = $7,670.00 (10.23% of wages)
After 18 of 26 bi-weekly paychecks, $4,800 has been withheld; the stub shows $230 a paycheck, so 8 more add $1,840.
Projected withholding = $6,640.00, a shortfall of $1,030.00
Extra withholding = $1,030.00 ÷ 8 = $128.75 per paycheck in Step 4(c)
Example 2: married filing jointly, $120,000, two children
Taxable income = 120,000 − 32,200 = $87,800.00
Tax before credits $10,040.00; Child Tax Credit 2 × $2,200 = $4,400
Tax after credits = $5,640.00
If withholding for the year is on track to be $5,640.00 plus $3,600, the couple would get about a $3,600.00 refund. They could reduce withholding by entering the credits in Step 3 of the W-4 to keep more in each paycheck instead.
Example 3: two jobs, both with default W-4s
A single filer earns $60,000 at one job and $30,000 at another:
Tax on the combined $90,000: taxable income $73,900, tax $10,970.00
Job 1 withholds as if $60,000 were the only income: about $5,020.00
Job 2 also applies the full standard deduction and the low brackets: about $1,420.00
Total withheld ≈ $6,440.00, a shortfall of about $4,530.00
Spread over 26 paychecks, that's $174.23 of extra withholding per paycheck, entered on one job's W-4 in Step 4(c), or use the Step 2 checkbox on both W-4s.
Example 4: a bonus withheld at 22%
A $5,000 bonus withheld at the 22% supplemental rate has $1,100.00 of federal tax taken. If your top bracket is 12%, the actual tax on the bonus is about $600.00, so the extra $500.00 comes back as part of your refund.
The W-4 steps
Step 1: personal information and filing status.
Step 2: multiple jobs or a working spouse. Use the IRS estimator, the worksheet, or tick the box if there are only two jobs with similar pay.
Step 3: dependants and other credits.
Step 4(a): other income without withholding. 4(b): deductions beyond the standard deduction. 4(c): extra withholding per paycheck.
Step 5: sign.
Since 2020 the W-4 doesn't use allowances. You can submit a new W-4 at any time; changes usually apply from the next payroll.
Understanding your results
A projection, not a return. It's based on the year's figures you enter; a bonus, job change or new child can change it.
Underpayment penalty safe harbors: you generally avoid a penalty if withholding and timely estimated payments cover at least 90% of this year's tax or 100% of last year's (110% if last year's AGI was over $150,000).
Bonuses are often withheld at a flat 22% supplemental rate, which may be too little or too much for you.
State withholding is separate and uses state forms.
Tips and common mistakes
Two jobs, two default W-4s. Each employer withholds as if it's your only job, often leaving you short. Use Step 2.
Forgetting side income that has no withholding.
Not updating after life changes: marriage, divorce, a new child or buying a home.
Claiming credits twice when both spouses enter them on their W-4s.
Notes for Canadian and UK workers
Canada: the equivalent form is the TD1 (federal plus a provincial version), which sets your personal tax credits. If you have two jobs, you generally claim the basic personal amount with only one employer, and you can request extra deductions on the form.
UK: there's no form to fill in each year. HMRC issues a tax code to each employer, such as 1257L for the standard Personal Allowance, and second jobs usually get a BR code (all taxed at the basic rate). Check your code in your HMRC personal tax account if your pay looks wrong.
Frequently asked questions
How do I know if I'm withholding enough?
Compare projected withholding with projected tax using your latest pay stub, as this calculator does.
What do I put in Step 4(c)?
The extra amount per paycheck needed to cover any shortfall.
Can I change my W-4 mid-year?
Yes, at any time, by giving your employer a new form.
Is it better to get a refund or owe?
Owing a small amount means you kept your money during the year, but owing too much can bring penalties.
Does the W-4 affect Social Security and Medicare?
No. FICA is withheld at fixed rates regardless of the W-4.
Where can I get an official estimate?
The IRS Tax Withholding Estimator on irs.gov.

Title tag
Army Body Fat Calculator (Tape Test Estimate) | FigSumo (55 chars)
Meta description
Estimate body fat with the US Army circumference method from height, neck, waist and hip. Explains how the tape is measured. (124 chars)
Country
global
Status
keep
Body words
1,020 (minimum 1,000)
H1: Army Body Fat Calculator
The U.S. Army estimates body fat with a tape measure rather than scales or scans, so soldiers can be assessed quickly anywhere. This calculator applies the Department of Defense circumference equations, which use height and neck and waist measurements (plus hips for women), to estimate body fat percentage. It's also a useful home estimate for anyone, as long as you understand its limits.
How to use this calculator
1. Sex: the equations differ for men and women.
2. Units: imperial (inches) or metric (centimetres).
3. Height: without shoes.
4. Neck: measured just below the larynx (Adam's apple), with the tape sloping slightly down to the front.
5. Abdomen / waist: for men, at the navel; for women, at the narrowest point of the natural waist (as in the two-site method).
6. Hip (women only): at the widest point of the buttocks.
Measure on bare skin, standing relaxed, without pulling the tape tight; take each measurement three times and average them.
Results: body fat percentage with a note that official screening uses age-specific maximum standards.
The formulas (two-site DoD circumference method)
All measurements in inches:
Men:   %BF = 86.010 × log10(waist − neck) − 70.041 × log10(height) + 36.76
Women: %BF = 163.205 × log10(waist + hip − neck) − 97.684 × log10(height) − 78.387
These are the Hodgdon and Beckett equations developed for the U.S. Navy and used across the DoD. Metric inputs are converted to inches first (175 cm = 68.9 in).
Note on the current Army method: in 2023 the Army adopted a one-site tape test that uses abdominal circumference and body weight [VERIFY current regulation]. This page's calculator currently implements the two-site method; the one-site method is being added.
Worked examples
Example 1: man, 69 in tall, neck 15 in, waist 34 in
waist − neck = 19; log10(19) = 1.2788
log10(69) = 1.8388
%BF = 86.010 × 1.2788 − 70.041 × 1.8388 + 36.76 = 18.0%
If his waist were 36 in, the estimate would rise to 21.7%. The waist measurement drives most of the change.
Example 2: woman, 64 in tall, neck 13 in, waist 30 in, hip 38 in
waist + hip − neck = 55
%BF = 163.205 × log10(55) − 97.684 × log10(64) − 78.387 = 29.2%
Example 3: one-site method (for comparison)
Using the one-site male equation [VERIFY coefficients] for a 180 lb man with a 34 in abdomen: −26.97 − 0.12 × 180 + 1.99 × 34 = 19.1%. Different equations can give somewhat different results for the same person.
Example 4: metric measurements
A man 180 cm tall with a 40 cm neck and a 90 cm waist:
In inches: height 70.87, neck 15.75, waist 35.43
%BF = 86.010 × log10(19.69) − 70.041 × log10(70.87) + 36.76 = 18.5%
The widely quoted metric version of the Navy equation, 495 ÷ (1.0324 − 0.19077 × log10(waist − neck) + 0.15456 × log10(height)) − 450, gives 18.4% for the same person. The small difference comes from how the two versions were fitted, so use one version consistently when tracking change.
Example 5: woman, metric
160 cm tall, neck 32 cm, waist 74 cm, hip 98 cm. In inches: 62.99, 12.60, 29.13 and 38.58. Waist + hip − neck = 55.12 in, giving 30.0%.
Understanding your results
It's an estimate. Circumference equations typically differ from laboratory methods such as DEXA by a few percentage points for individuals, more for very muscular or very lean people.
Consistency matters more than precision. Use the same tape, time of day and technique to track change.
Army standards set maximum body fat percentages that vary by age group and sex. Soldiers who exceed the screening table weight for their height are taped; those over the allowable body fat may be enrolled in a body composition program. Check the current regulation for the limits that apply [VERIFY current AR 600-9 tables].
General health ranges: for non-military use, see the body fat calculator, which explains ranges and other methods.
Measurement tips
Use a non-stretch tape, read to the nearest half inch (or nearest 0.5 cm).
Don't suck in your stomach or flex your neck.
Measure the neck below the larynx, the male abdomen at the navel, and the female waist at its narrowest point.
Repeat until three measurements agree within a quarter inch.
Tips and common mistakes
Mixing units: entering centimetres while inches is selected.
Measuring over clothing.
Comparing results from different equations as if they were identical.
Treating the result as a diagnosis. It's a field estimate of body composition.
Notes for Canada and UK users
The equations here are US Department of Defense standards, and the age-group limits belong to US Army regulations. The Canadian Armed Forces and the UK Armed Forces set their own fitness and body-composition rules, so US limits don't apply to them [VERIFY current CAF and MOD policies]. Civilians in any country can still use the tape method as a free home estimate, as long as they measure the same way each time.
Frequently asked questions
How does the Army calculate body fat?
With a tape-measure method: historically the two-site neck and waist (plus hip for women) equations, and since 2023 a one-site abdominal method [VERIFY].
Is the Army tape test accurate?
Reasonably for groups, less precise for individuals. It can underestimate or overestimate by several percentage points.
Where do I measure my waist for the tape test?
Men at the navel; women at the narrowest point between the ribs and hips for the two-site method.
What is the maximum body fat for the Army?
It depends on age and sex; check the current Army regulation.
Can I use this if I'm not in the military?
Yes, as a convenient home estimate.
Why does my neck measurement matter?
A larger neck relative to the waist suggests more lean mass, so it lowers the estimate.

Blood Alcohol (BAC) Calculator

Title tag
Blood Alcohol Content (BAC) Estimator | FigSumo (47 chars)
Meta description
Rough BAC estimate from weight, sex, drinks and time using the Widmark formula. Never use it to decide whether you are safe or legal to drive. (142 chars)
Country
global
Status
keep
Body words
1,061 (minimum 1,000)
H1: Blood Alcohol (BAC) Calculator
Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is the percentage of your blood that is alcohol. This calculator estimates BAC from the number of standard drinks, your body weight and sex, and the time since you started drinking, using the Widmark formula. It's an educational estimate only: many factors affect real BAC, and no calculator can tell you whether you're safe to drive.
How to use this calculator
1. Sex: men and women distribute alcohol differently on average.
2. Units and body weight.
3. Standard drinks consumed: the calculator counts each standard drink as 14 grams of pure alcohol (the US definition).
4. Hours since first drink.
Results: estimated BAC (%), alcohol consumed in grams and a safety note.
The formula (Widmark)
BAC (%) = [Alcohol (g) ÷ (Body weight (g) × r)] × 100 − 0.015 × Hours
Alcohol: standard drinks × 14 g
r: the Widmark factor, the share of body weight in which alcohol distributes: 0.68 for men and 0.55 for women (averages)
0.015: an average elimination rate of 0.015 percentage points per hour
The result can't go below zero.
What's a standard drink (US)? About 12 fl oz of 5% beer, 5 fl oz of 12% wine, or 1.5 fl oz of 40% spirits. Many real drinks are larger: a strong craft beer or a generous pour of wine can be 1.5 to 2 standard drinks.
Worked examples
Example 1: man, 80 kg, 4 drinks over 2 hours
Alcohol = 4 × 14 = 56 g
Peak contribution = 56 ÷ (80,000 × 0.68) × 100 = 0.103%
Minus 2 × 0.015 = 0.030
Estimated BAC = 0.073%
At 0.015 an hour, it would take about 4.9 more hours to fall to zero.
In imperial units, 180 lb is about 81.6 kg.
Example 2: woman, 65 kg, 3 drinks over 1 hour
Estimated BAC = 0.102%, falling to zero in about 6.8 hours.
Understanding your results
Effects begin well below legal limits. Judgment, reaction time and coordination start to be affected at low BACs, around 0.02% to 0.05%.
Individual variation is large. Food in the stomach, drinking speed, medications, body composition, age, liver function and genetics all change real BAC. The elimination rate varies roughly from 0.010 to 0.020 per hour between people.
BAC can still be rising after you stop drinking, as alcohol is absorbed.
Only time lowers BAC. Coffee, cold showers and food after drinking don't speed elimination.
Legal limits for driving
United States: 0.08% in every state except Utah, which uses 0.05%. Commercial drivers: 0.04%. Drivers under 21: zero tolerance laws (typically 0.00% to 0.02%).
Canada: 0.08% is the federal criminal limit; most provinces impose administrative penalties from 0.05%. Many provinces require zero BAC for new and young drivers.
United Kingdom: 0.08% (80 mg per 100 ml of blood) in England, Wales and Northern Ireland; 0.05% in Scotland.
Being under the limit doesn't mean you're safe or legal to drive if you're impaired. The safest choice is not to drive after drinking.
Example 3: three UK pints
A pint (568 ml) of 5% beer contains 568 × 0.05 × 0.789 = 22.4 g of alcohol, which is 1.6 US standard drinks or 2.8 UK units. For a 75 kg man who drinks three pints over three hours:
Alcohol: 3 × 22.4 = 67.2 g, so enter 4.8 standard drinks
67.2 ÷ (75,000 × 0.68) × 100 − 0.015 × 3 = 0.087%
That's above the drink-drive limit in Scotland (0.05%) and in the rest of the UK (0.08%), even though "three pints" sounds moderate.
Units of measurement for BAC
US laws express BAC as grams of alcohol per 100 ml of blood, written as a percentage (0.08%). Canadian and UK laws write the same limit as 80 mg of alcohol per 100 ml of blood. The UK also sets breath limits: 35 micrograms of alcohol per 100 ml of breath in England, Wales and Northern Ireland, and 22 micrograms in Scotland. Roadside breath tests estimate blood alcohol from breath, so results can differ slightly from a blood test.
Standard drinks in other countries
The calculator uses the US 14 g standard drink. In Canada a standard drink is about 13.45 g of alcohol [VERIFY], and in the UK one unit is 8 g (10 ml) of alcohol; a pint of 5% beer is about 2.8 units (about 22 g). Convert to US standard drinks by dividing grams of alcohol by 14.
Health guidance
United States: the Dietary Guidelines advise that adults who choose to drink limit intake to 2 drinks or fewer a day for men and 1 or fewer for women [VERIFY current guideline wording].
Canada: Canada's Guidance on Alcohol and Health (2023) describes risk rising with each drink, with 2 or fewer drinks a week as low risk.
United Kingdom: the UK Chief Medical Officers advise not regularly drinking more than 14 units a week.
Tips and common mistakes
Counting glasses instead of standard drinks.
Assuming you're fine after a meal. Food slows absorption but doesn't remove alcohol.
Driving the morning after a heavy night; BAC may still be above the limit.
Mixing alcohol with medication without checking interactions.
Frequently asked questions
How accurate is a BAC calculator?
It gives a rough average estimate. Your actual BAC could be significantly higher or lower.
How long does it take for alcohol to leave the body?
On average about 0.015 percentage points of BAC per hour, so a BAC of 0.08% takes roughly 5 hours to reach zero.
What is the legal limit?
0.08% in most of the US, Canada (criminal) and England, Wales and Northern Ireland; 0.05% in Utah and Scotland.
Why do women reach higher BAC than men?
On average, women have less body water per kilogram, so alcohol is more concentrated.
Can I sober up faster?
No. Only time reduces BAC.
Is it safe to drive under the limit?
Not necessarily. Impairment begins at low levels.

Calculate your Body Mass Index in kg/cm or lb/ft-in, see the adult category, the healthy weight range for your height and child BMI-for-age guidance. (149 chars)

H1: BMI Calculator
Body Mass Index (BMI) compares your weight with your height. It's quick to calculate and widely used to screen for weight categories that may be linked to health risks. It doesn't measure body fat directly, and it doesn't diagnose anything. This calculator gives your BMI in metric or imperial units, the adult category, the weight range that corresponds to a healthy BMI for your height, and separate guidance for children and teens.
How to use this calculator
1. Choose metric (kg, cm) or imperial (lb, ft and in).
2. Enter your height and weight.
3. Enter age, and sex for under-20s. Children's BMI is interpreted with sex- and age-specific percentiles, not adult cut-offs.
4. Optional (UK users): tick the box if you are from a South Asian, Chinese, other Asian, Middle Eastern, Black African or African-Caribbean background, to see the NHS's lower thresholds.
The formula
Metric:   BMI = weight (kg) ÷ height (m)²
Imperial: BMI = 703 × weight (lb) ÷ height (in)²
The 703 converts pounds and inches to the same units as kg/m². The two formulas agree to within rounding.
Healthy weight range for your height (adults): weight = BMI × height², calculated at BMI 18.5 and just under 25.
Adult categories (CDC, ages 20+):

For some ethnic groups, the NHS notes that health risks start at a lower BMI. It treats 23 to 27.4 as overweight and 27.5 or above as obese.
Ages 2–19: the CDC uses BMI-for-age percentiles. Below the 5th percentile is underweight; 5th to under the 85th is healthy weight; 85th to under the 95th is overweight; the 95th or above is obesity.
Worked examples
Example 1: metric. Height 178 cm (1.78 m), weight 82 kg.
1.78² = 3.1684
BMI = 82 ÷ 3.1684 = 25.88, in the overweight category (25 to under 30)
Healthy-weight range at 1.78 m: 18.5 × 3.1684 = 58.6 kg up to about 24.9 × 3.1684 = 78.9 kg
Example 2: imperial. Height 5 ft 10 in (70 in), weight 180 lb.
70² = 4,900
BMI = 703 × 180 ÷ 4,900 = 25.82, also overweight
Healthy-weight range at 5 ft 10 in: about 129 lb to 173 lb
As a cross-check, the CDC's own example for an adult who is 5 ft 9 in gives a healthy weight range of 125 to 168 lb. One inch taller moves both ends up by a few pounds, which matches our figures.
Example 3: stones and pounds (UK). 10 st 10 lb is 150 lb (68.0 kg); 5 ft 6 in is 167.6 cm. BMI = 68.0 ÷ 1.676² = 24.2, in the healthy weight category.

Understanding your results
BMI is a screening measure. The CDC says it should be considered with other factors when assessing someone's health. Waist size, blood pressure, blood tests, activity and family history all matter.
Muscle and frame: muscular people can have a high BMI without excess fat. Older adults can have a "healthy" BMI while carrying more fat and less muscle.
Not for pregnancy: BMI categories don't apply during pregnancy.
Children: a single BMI number means different things at different ages. The calculator shows the percentile and category, and a doctor should interpret growth over time.
If your result concerns you, talk to a healthcare professional. This calculator doesn't diagnose conditions or recommend treatment.
Country notes
US: categories follow the CDC definitions for adults 20 and older.
UK: the NHS uses the same adult bands, with lower thresholds for the ethnic groups listed above. NHS guidance also uses waist-to-height ratio alongside BMI.
Canada: Health Canada's adult BMI classification uses the same cut-offs (VERIFY citation before publishing).
Worldwide: the WHO defines adult overweight as BMI ≥ 25 and obesity as BMI ≥ 30.
Tips and common mistakes
Measuring height with shoes on. It lowers your BMI slightly.
Using adult categories for children. Under-20s need BMI-for-age percentiles.
Treating BMI as a diagnosis. It's a screening measure; waist size adds context.
Ignoring ethnicity-specific thresholds if they apply to you.
Frequently asked questions
What is a healthy BMI?
For most adults, 18.5 to under 25. For people from certain ethnic backgrounds, the NHS suggests risk rises from 23.
Is BMI accurate?
It is a useful population screening tool, but it doesn't distinguish fat from muscle or show where fat is stored. Measures such as waist circumference or a body fat estimate add context.
Why does the calculator ask my age?
Because under-20s are assessed with age- and sex-specific percentiles. Adult categories only apply from age 20 in the CDC system.
What's the BMI formula in pounds and inches?
BMI = 703 × weight in pounds ÷ (height in inches)². For 180 lb at 70 inches: 703 × 180 ÷ 4,900 = 25.82.
Can I use BMI during pregnancy?
No. Pregnancy changes weight in ways BMI isn't designed to interpret. Pre-pregnancy BMI is sometimes used to guide weight-gain advice; ask your midwife or doctor.
My BMI is in the overweight range but I exercise a lot. Should I worry?
Not necessarily. BMI can't tell muscle from fat. Discuss your overall health with a professional rather than relying on one number.

https://figsumo.com/bmr-calculator
Title tag
BMR Calculator: Basal Metabolic Rate (Mifflin-St Jeor) | FigSumo (64 chars)
Meta description
Calculate your basal metabolic rate with Mifflin-St Jeor, revised Harris-Benedict or Katch-McArdle, in kcal or kJ, and see how activity changes daily needs. (156 chars)
Country
global
Status
keep
Body words
1,031 (minimum 1,000)
H1: BMR Calculator
Your basal metabolic rate (BMR) is the energy your body would use in a day at complete rest, just to keep you alive: breathing, circulation and keeping your organs working. For most people it is the largest part of daily calorie use. BMR can't be measured at home, so this calculator estimates it with published equations based on your size, age and sex. It shows three equations side by side so you can see how much they differ.
How to use this calculator
1. Choose metric or imperial. Imperial inputs are converted exactly (1 lb = 0.45359237 kg; 1 in = 2.54 cm).
2. Enter age, sex, height and weight.
3. Optional: enter a body-fat percentage to add the Katch-McArdle estimate, which uses lean mass instead of sex and age.
4. Choose kcal or kJ for the output.
5. Below the result, a table multiplies your BMR by standard activity factors to give daily needs.
The formula
Mifflin-St Jeor (1990), the default:
Men:   BMR = 10W + 6.25H − 5A + 5
Women: BMR = 10W + 6.25H − 5A − 161
Revised Harris-Benedict (Roza & Shizgal, 1984):
Men:   BMR = 88.362 + 13.397W + 4.799H − 5.677A
Women: BMR = 447.593 + 9.247W + 3.098H − 4.330A
Katch-McArdle (needs body-fat %):
BMR = 370 + 21.6 × LBM,   LBM = W × (1 − body fat % ÷ 100)
W: weight in kg
H: height in cm
A: age in years
LBM: lean body mass in kg
Daily needs: BMR × 1.2 (sedentary) up to 1.9 (extra active).
Worked examples
Example 1: man, 40, 180 cm, 85 kg.
Mifflin-St Jeor: 10 × 85 + 6.25 × 180 − 5 × 40 + 5 = 850 + 1,125 − 200 + 5 = 1,780 kcal/day (7,448 kJ)
Revised Harris-Benedict: 88.362 + 1,138.745 + 863.82 − 227.08 = 1,863.8 kcal/day
If his body fat is 19.5%: LBM = 85 × 0.805 = 68.4 kg, and Katch-McArdle gives 370 + 21.6 × 68.4 ≈ 1,847 kcal/day
The three estimates span about 84 kcal, under 5%.
Daily needs from the Mifflin BMR:
Sedentary: 1,780 × 1.2 = 2,136 kcal
Very active: 1,780 × 1.725 = 3,070.5 kcal
Example 2: the same man in imperial units. 187 lb and 5 ft 11 in convert to 84.82 kg and 180.34 cm. Mifflin gives 1,780.3 kcal/day. The tiny difference from Example 1 is only because 187 lb and 5 ft 11 in are not exactly 85 kg and 180 cm.
Example 3: woman, 28, 163 cm, 58 kg, 26% body fat.
Mifflin-St Jeor: 580 + 1,018.75 − 140 − 161 = 1,298 kcal/day (5,430 kJ)
Revised Harris-Benedict: 1,368 kcal/day
Katch-McArdle: LBM = 58 × 0.74 = 42.9 kg; 370 + 21.6 × 42.9 = 1,297 kcal/day
Here Mifflin-St Jeor and Katch-McArdle agree almost exactly, while Harris-Benedict is about 70 kcal higher.
How BMR changes with age (Mifflin-St Jeor)

Woman, 165 cm, 65 kg

In the equation, each extra year lowers BMR by exactly 5 kcal for the same height and weight. Real changes also depend on how much muscle you keep, which is why strength training matters as you get older.
Understanding your results
BMR is an estimate. Predictive equations are accurate on average, not for every person. Roza and Shizgal reported a precision of about ±14% for the revised Harris-Benedict equations. An individual's measured value can differ noticeably from any formula.
What raises or lowers BMR: more lean mass raises it. Age tends to lower it, mostly through loss of muscle. Illness, fever, some medications and thyroid function can change it significantly.
BMR vs RMR: "resting metabolic rate" is measured under less strict conditions and is usually a little higher. The equations here are often used interchangeably for both.
Using the number: BMR by itself is not a daily calorie target. Multiply by your activity level, or use the calorie calculator.
Country notes
Units: US users typically enter pounds and feet/inches; UK users may use stone. The imperial mode accepts stone + lb (VERIFY: add stone input in T-223). Canada mostly uses metric. Energy appears as kcal on US and Canadian labels, and as kJ and kcal on UK and EU labels.
The equations are not country-specific. They were developed mainly in North American adult populations, so accuracy may differ in other groups.
Tips and common mistakes
Treating BMR as a calorie target. Multiply by an activity factor first.
Mixing units. Use kg and cm, or switch to imperial mode.
Using an outdated weight. Recalculate after a change of a few kilograms.
Choosing Katch-McArdle without a reliable body-fat figure. Errors in body fat feed straight into the result.
Frequently asked questions
What is a normal BMR?
There's no single normal value. BMR scales with body size and lean mass, and it differs by sex and age. That's why the calculator asks for all four. Compare your result with your own measured weight trend rather than with someone else's number.
Which BMR formula should I use?
Mifflin-St Jeor is widely used for healthy adults. Use Katch-McArdle if you have a reliable body-fat measurement. Showing all three gives you a sense of the uncertainty.
Does muscle increase BMR?
Lean tissue uses more energy at rest than fat tissue, so more muscle generally means a higher BMR. This is why Katch-McArdle uses lean mass.
Why does BMR fall with age?
Partly because of changes in body composition, mainly less muscle, and partly because of changes in organ metabolism. The equations include an age term to reflect this on average.
Can I eat my BMR calories to lose weight?
BMR is the energy for rest only. Eating far below your total needs can be hard to sustain and isn't appropriate for everyone. Speak to a healthcare professional before starting a restrictive diet.
Is BMR the same as metabolism?
BMR is one part of metabolism. Total daily energy also includes the energy used to digest food and all physical activity.

Body Fat Calculator

Title tag
Body Fat Calculator: U.S. Navy Tape-Measure Method | FigSumo (60 chars)
Meta description
Estimate body fat percentage from height, neck, waist and (for women) hip measurements using the U.S. Navy circumference method, plus fat mass and lean mass. (157 chars)
Country
global (cm/in)
Status
keep
Body words
1,075 (minimum 1,000)
H1: Body Fat Calculator
Body fat percentage is the share of your weight that is fat tissue. It tells you something BMI can't: two people with the same BMI can have very different amounts of fat and muscle. The most accurate measurements need lab equipment such as DXA scans. This calculator uses the U.S. Navy circumference method, a published equation that estimates body fat from a few tape-measure readings.
How to use this calculator
1. Choose cm or inches.
2. Enter sex and height.
3. Measure and enter, to the nearest 0.5 cm or ¼ inch:
Neck: just below the larynx (Adam's apple), with the tape sloping slightly down to the front.
Waist: for men, horizontally at the navel. For women, at the narrowest point of the abdomen.
Hips (women only): at the widest point of the buttocks.
4. Optional: enter your weight to see fat mass and lean mass in kg or lb.
5. Measure on bare skin with the tape snug but not compressing. Take the average of two or three readings.
The formula
The Navy method comes from Hodgdon and Beckett (Naval Health Research Center, 1984). With all measurements in inches:
Men:   %BF = 86.010 × log10(waist − neck) − 70.041 × log10(height) + 36.76
Women: %BF = 163.205 × log10(waist + hip − neck) − 97.684 × log10(height) − 78.387
log10: base-10 logarithm
waist, neck, hip, height: circumferences and height in inches
If you enter centimetres, the calculator converts them to inches (÷ 2.54) and then applies the same equations.
A note on the metric version. Many websites use a different, density-based metric form of these equations. It gives results about 0.1–0.3 percentage points different from the inch version (see the examples). We use the inch version for both unit systems so that the result doesn't change when you switch units.
Fat and lean mass (if weight is given):
Fat mass  = weight × %BF ÷ 100
Lean mass = weight − fat mass
Worked examples
Example 1: man. Height 178 cm (70.08 in), neck 39 cm (15.35 in), waist 90 cm (35.43 in).
waist − neck = 20.08 in → log10 = 1.3027
log10(70.08) = 1.8456
%BF = 86.010 × 1.3027 − 70.041 × 1.8456 + 36.76 = 19.5% (19.54)
The density-based metric form gives 19.43%
At 85 kg: fat mass ≈ 16.6 kg, lean mass ≈ 68.4 kg
Example 2: woman. Height 165 cm, neck 33 cm, waist 76 cm, hips 100 cm.
waist + hip − neck = 143 cm = 56.30 in
%BF = 163.205 × log10(56.30) − 97.684 × log10(64.96) − 78.387 = 30.2% (30.24)
The density-based metric form gives 29.93%
At 68 kg: fat mass ≈ 20.6 kg, lean mass ≈ 47.4 kg
Example 3: man, imperial. Height 5 ft 10 in (70 in), neck 16 in, waist 38 in.
waist − neck = 22 in → log10 = 1.3424
%BF = 86.010 × 1.3424 − 70.041 × 1.8451 + 36.76 = 23.0%
At 200 lb: fat mass ≈ 46.0 lb, lean mass ≈ 154.0 lb
How much the waist matters
For a man 70 in tall with a 15 in neck, each 2 in of waist changes the estimate by roughly 3 to 5 percentage points:

Because the neck measurement is subtracted from the waist, a thicker neck (often a sign of more muscle) lowers the estimate. Measure both carefully: a quarter-inch error in the neck matters as much as one in the waist.
Understanding your results
It's an estimate. Circumference equations are fitted to population data. Your own value from a lab method could be several points higher or lower, especially if your fat distribution is unusual for your sex.
Consistency matters more than precision. If you track changes, measure the same way, at the same time of day, each time. A trend over weeks is more meaningful than a single reading.
There's no single universal healthy range. Different organisations publish different reference ranges by sex and age. If you want to know what your number means for your health, ask a healthcare professional.
Implausible inputs: if the waist measurement is not larger than the neck (or, for women, waist + hip is not larger than the neck), the equations can't be applied, and the calculator will ask you to check your measurements.
Country notes
U.S. military: service standards and approved methods have changed over time, and the Army introduced a different method in recent years. This page uses the original Navy equations. Service members should follow their branch's current instructions (VERIFY current DoD/Army method before adding a military mode).
UK/Canada: the method is the same anywhere. Use cm or inches as you prefer.
Tips and common mistakes
Measuring over clothing. Use bare skin.
Pulling the tape tight. Keep it snug but not compressing.
Measuring at different points each time. Note where you measured.
Comparing results from different methods. Tape, scales and DEXA give different numbers.
Frequently asked questions
How accurate is the Navy body fat method?
It's reasonable for tracking trends and for population screening. It is less accurate for an individual than DXA, hydrostatic weighing or air-displacement methods.
Why do men and women use different formulas?
Fat is distributed differently on average. The women's equation includes hip circumference to account for that.
Why does my result differ from another website's?
Usually because the other site uses the density-based metric form, or measures at a different place. Our examples show the size of the difference between the two forms.
Can I use this if I'm very muscular?
Yes. That is one advantage over BMI. Very large neck measurements, though, can lower the estimate, so compare it with other methods if possible.
Does body fat percentage replace BMI?
They answer different questions. BMI relates weight to height; body fat estimates composition. Using both, along with waist measurement, gives a fuller picture.
How often should I measure?
Every few weeks is plenty for tracking. Day-to-day changes are mostly measurement noise.

Body Frame Size Calculator (Wrist Measurement) | FigSumo (56 chars)
Meta description
Estimate small, medium or large frame size from height and wrist circumference. Explains what frame size does and does not tell you. (132 chars)

1,025 (minimum 1,000)
H1: Body Frame Size Calculator
"Body type" usually refers to the three somatotypes popularised in the 1940s, ectomorph (lean, narrow), mesomorph (muscular, broad) and endomorph (rounder, stores fat more easily), along with frame size, the size of your skeleton. This calculator estimates your frame size from your height and wrist circumference, calculates your BMI, and gives a descriptive body-type label. It's a rough, descriptive tool, not a scientific classification.
How to use this calculator
1. Sex.
2. Units: metric or imperial.
3. Weight and height.
4. Wrist circumference: measure around the wrist just above the wrist bone (toward the hand), using a flexible tape, in the same units as height.
Results: suggested body type, frame size (from the ratio of height to wrist), and BMI with its category.
How it works
Frame size uses the ratio r = height ÷ wrist circumference:
r value
Men
Women
Small frame
above 10.9
above 11.0
Medium frame
9.6 to 10.9
9.6 to 11.0
Large frame
below 9.6
below 9.6
A larger wrist relative to height gives a smaller r and a larger frame.
BMI = weight (kg) ÷ height (m)².
Body-type label:
BMI under 18.5 → "ectomorph-leaning"
BMI 25 or more → "endomorph-leaning"
Otherwise, a large frame → "mesomorph-leaning"; small or medium → "mesomorph / balanced"
Because the label is based on BMI and frame size, it describes your current size and build, not a fixed type you were born with.
Worked examples
Example 1: man, 178 cm, wrist 17 cm, 75 kg
r = 178 ÷ 17 = 10.47 → Medium frame
BMI = 75 ÷ 1.78² = 23.7 (healthy weight range)
Label: mesomorph / balanced
Example 2: woman, 163 cm, wrist 14.5 cm, 58 kg
r = 11.24 → Small frame
BMI = 21.8
Label: mesomorph / balanced (small frame)
Example 3: man, 180 cm, wrist 19.5 cm, 95 kg
r = 9.23 → large frame
BMI = 29.3 → endomorph-leaning label
A heavily muscled person with a high BMI may get an "endomorph" label even with low body fat. That's a limitation of using BMI. Check body fat with the body fat calculator for a better picture.
Example 4: two more profiles
Man, 185 cm, wrist 18 cm, 82 kg: r = 10.28 (medium frame), BMI 24.0 → mesomorph / balanced
Woman, 170 cm, wrist 15 cm, 80 kg: r = 11.33 (small frame), BMI 27.7 → endomorph-leaning
The woman's label comes from her BMI of 25 or more, not from her frame, which shows how strongly BMI drives the result.
What somatotypes can and can't tell you
The somatotype idea came from psychologist William Sheldon, whose claims linking body shape to personality have been discredited. Sports scientists later developed the Heath-Carter method, which rates each component from skinfolds, bone breadths and girths; it's used to describe athletes, not to predict health. Simple online body-type quizzes and calculators, including this one, give a broad description at best.
What matters more for health:
Body fat and where it's stored. Waist size and waist-to-height ratio are linked to health risks; see the waist-to-height ratio calculator.
Fitness and strength, which can be improved regardless of body type.
Diet and activity habits.
Using frame size
Frame size is sometimes used to adjust "ideal weight" ranges: a person with a large frame may sit toward the upper end of a healthy-weight range and a small frame toward the lower end. See the ideal weight calculator and the healthy weight calculator.
Measuring your wrist
Use a flexible tape (or a strip of paper you then measure with a ruler).
Wrap it around the smallest part of the wrist, just above the bony bump on the little-finger side, toward the hand.
Keep the tape snug but not tight. A 6¾-inch wrist is 17.1 cm.
Tips and common mistakes
Mixing units for height and wrist. The ratio only works if both are in the same units.
Treating the label as permanent. Training and diet change body composition.
Choosing a diet or workout by somatotype alone. There's little evidence that somatotype-specific diets work better.
Notes for US, Canada and UK users
Frame size from wrist measurements was popularised in the US through the Metropolitan Life height-weight tables of the 1980s, which gave separate ranges for small, medium and large frames. Today the CDC, Health Canada and the NHS don't use frame size in public health advice. They combine BMI with waist circumference:
US (NIH) and Canada: health risk rises with a waist above 102 cm (40 in) for men and 88 cm (35 in) for women.
UK (NHS): risk is increased above 94 cm (37 in) for men and 80 cm (31.5 in) for women, and NICE also recommends keeping your waist below half your height.
Elbow breadth, measured with calipers across the bent elbow, is another way to estimate frame size and is less affected by body fat than the wrist, but it needs a measuring tool that most people don't have at home.
Frequently asked questions
How do I know my body type?
This calculator gives a rough description from your BMI and frame size. A formal somatotype assessment requires anthropometric measurements by a trained professional.
What is my frame size?
Divide your height by your wrist circumference: above about 11 is small and below 9.6 is large, with medium in between (thresholds vary by sex and source).
Can I change my body type?
Your skeleton and frame don't change, but body fat and muscle do, so a descriptive label can change.
Is mesomorph the best body type?
No body type is "best". Health depends on fitness, body fat distribution and habits.
Are somatotypes scientific?
The original theory isn't supported. The Heath-Carter method is a descriptive tool used in sports science.
Does frame size affect healthy weight?
It can shift where you fall within a healthy range, but BMI ranges themselves don't change with frame size.

Title tag
Body Surface Area (BSA) Calculator: Mosteller & DuBois | FigSumo (64 chars)
Meta description
Calculate body surface area in m² from height and weight with the Mosteller, DuBois and other published formulas, side by side. (127 chars)

1,041 (minimum 1,000)
H1: Body Surface Area Calculator
Body surface area (BSA) is the total area of the outer surface of the body, in square metres. Doctors and pharmacists use it to dose some medicines, especially chemotherapy, to index measurements such as cardiac output and kidney function, and to estimate fluid needs in burns care. This calculator estimates BSA from height and weight using the Mosteller formula.
How to use this calculator
1. Units: metric (kg, cm) or imperial (lb, ft and in).
2. Weight.
3. Height.
Result: body surface area (Mosteller) in m².
The formula
Mosteller (1987):
BSA (m²) = √(Height (cm) × Weight (kg) ÷ 3,600)
It's the most widely used formula because it's simple and agrees closely with older formulas for most adults.
Other formulas you may see:
Du Bois and Du Bois (1916): BSA = 0.007184 × W^0.425 × H^0.725
Haycock (1978), often used for children: BSA = 0.024265 × W^0.5378 × H^0.3964
Worked examples
Example 1: adult, 70 kg and 175 cm
175 × 70 = 12,250; ÷ 3,600 and square root
BSA = 1.84 m² (Mosteller)
Du Bois gives 1.85 m², Haycock 1.85 m²: very close for an average adult.
Example 2: imperial units
160 lb (72.6 kg) and 5 ft 6 in (167.6 cm):
BSA = 1.84 m²
Example 3: a child
20 kg and 110 cm:
BSA = 0.78 m²
Example 4: comparing formulas for a larger adult
120 kg and 185 cm:
Formula
BSA

2.42 m²

2.52 m²

2.50 m²
The formulas differ by up to 0.10 m² here, compared with about 0.01 m² for the 70 kg adult in Example 1. Du Bois, developed from just nine people, tends to give lower values at high body weights.
Example 5: a newborn
3.5 kg and 50 cm: √(50 × 3.5 ÷ 3,600) = 0.22 m², roughly one-eighth of an adult's.

Values are in m². For in-between heights and weights, enter your own figures above.
For the child in Example 3, Haycock and Du Bois both give 0.78 m² too, so the formulas agree closely at that size. For the newborn in Example 5, Haycock gives 0.224 m² and Du Bois 0.209 m², against Mosteller's 0.220 m². Paediatric teams usually specify which formula to use, because small differences matter more at low doses.
Understanding your results
Typical adult values are around 1.6 to 2.0 m²; the commonly quoted "average" is about 1.7 to 1.9 m².
Medication dosing: some drugs are prescribed in mg per m². For a drug dosed at 75 mg/m², a person with a BSA of 1.84 m² would be prescribed about 138 mg. Clinicians may cap or adjust doses, so never calculate a dose yourself.
Indexing: cardiac index (cardiac output ÷ BSA) and estimated GFR reported "per 1.73 m²" use BSA to compare people of different sizes. See the GFR calculator.
Formula differences are small for typical adults but larger at extremes of size, in young children and in people with obesity.
Using BSA-indexed values
Cardiac index: a cardiac output of 5.0 L/min in a person with a BSA of 1.84 m² gives a cardiac index of 5.0 ÷ 1.84 = 2.72 L/min/m². A commonly cited normal range is about 2.5 to 4.0 L/min/m².
Kidney function: laboratory eGFR is reported per 1.73 m². To convert an eGFR of 60 to an absolute value for someone with a BSA of 1.84 m²: 60 × 1.84 ÷ 1.73 = 63.8 mL/min. Some drug-dosing guidance uses the absolute value, which is a decision for the prescriber.
Notes for US, Canada and UK users
BSA-based dosing is used in cancer care in all three countries, but local policies differ on details such as which formula to use and whether to cap the BSA for very large patients. In the US, the American Society of Clinical Oncology recommends full weight-based chemotherapy doses for most patients with obesity rather than routinely capping BSA at 2.0 m². UK cancer networks and Canadian provincial cancer agencies publish their own protocols, which hospital pharmacists follow [VERIFY current local guidance]. Whatever your country, a BSA you calculate at home is for interest only.
When BSA is less useful
BSA doesn't distinguish fat from muscle, so in people with obesity it may overestimate the body mass that drugs actually distribute into; clinicians sometimes use adjusted body weight or other approaches. For burns, the percentage of BSA burned is usually estimated from charts such as the "rule of nines" or Lund and Browder charts rather than from this calculation.
Tips and common mistakes
Entering height in metres instead of centimetres (175, not 1.75).
Using pounds in a metric formula. Convert first or switch units.
Using an outdated weight for anything clinical.
Frequently asked questions
What is a normal body surface area?
For adults, roughly 1.6 to 2.0 m², depending on size.
Which BSA formula is best?
Mosteller is the most common and simplest. Hospitals may specify a particular formula for consistency.
Why is BSA used for chemotherapy?
BSA correlates with metabolic rate and drug clearance better than weight alone for some drugs.
How do I calculate BSA by hand?
Multiply height (cm) by weight (kg), divide by 3,600 and take the square root.
Is BSA the same as BMI?
No. BMI relates weight to height squared to screen weight status; BSA estimates surface area.
Can I use this for children?
Yes, the formula works for children, but paediatric dosing must be done by clinicians.

Title tag
Calorie Calculator: Daily Calories (TDEE) in kcal or kJ | FigSumo (65 chars)
Meta description
Estimate your daily calorie needs from age, sex, height, weight and activity using the Mifflin-St Jeor equation, in kcal or kJ, with weight-change targets. (155 chars)
Country
global (metric/imperial; kcal/kJ)
Status
keep
Body words
1,067 (minimum 1,000)
H1: Calorie Calculator
This calculator estimates how many calories (energy) your body uses in a day. It first works out the energy you burn at rest, then scales that up for your activity level. The result is a starting estimate for maintaining your weight, which you can adjust for a gradual loss or gain. Individual needs vary, so treat the number as a starting point and adjust it based on how your weight actually changes over several weeks.
How to use this calculator
1. Choose metric or imperial, and kcal or kJ for the result.
2. Enter age, sex, height and weight. The default equations were developed for adults, so the calculator is intended for ages 18 and over.
3. Choose an activity level:
Sedentary: little or no exercise
Light: exercise 1–3 days a week
Moderate: 3–5 days a week
Very active: 6–7 days a week
Extra active: physical job plus training
4. Optional: a body-fat percentage, to use the Katch-McArdle equation instead.
5. Choose a goal: maintain, lose or gain.
The formula
Step 1: resting energy (BMR) with Mifflin-St Jeor (1990):
Men:   BMR = 10 × weight(kg) + 6.25 × height(cm) − 5 × age(y) + 5
Women: BMR = 10 × weight(kg) + 6.25 × height(cm) − 5 × age(y) − 161
Step 2: total daily energy expenditure (TDEE):
TDEE = BMR × activity factor
Commonly used factors are 1.2 (sedentary), 1.375 (light), 1.55 (moderate), 1.725 (very active) and 1.9 (extra active).
Alternatives offered:
Revised Harris-Benedict (Roza & Shizgal, 1984):
men 88.362 + 13.397w + 4.799h − 5.677a
women 447.593 + 9.247w + 3.098h − 4.330a
Katch-McArdle: BMR = 370 + 21.6 × lean body mass (kg). This needs your body-fat percentage.
Units: 1 kcal = 4.184 kJ.
Worked examples
Example 1: woman, 35, 165 cm, 65 kg, moderately active.
BMR = 10 × 65 + 6.25 × 165 − 5 × 35 − 161 = 650 + 1,031.25 − 175 − 161 = 1,345.25 kcal/day
TDEE = 1,345.25 × 1.55 = 2,085 kcal/day (about 8,724 kJ)
The same person at other activity levels:

kcal/day

For comparison, the revised Harris-Benedict equation gives a BMR of 1,408 kcal for her, about 63 kcal higher. Different equations can disagree by this much.
Example 2: a modest calorie deficit. Aiming to eat about 500 kcal a day below the 2,085 maintenance estimate gives about 1,585 kcal/day. Research behind the NIH's Body Weight Planner (Hall et al., 2011) shows that weight loss slows over time as the body adapts. A fixed rule such as "3,500 kcal per pound" therefore overestimates long-term loss. The calculator links to that planner if you want a time-based projection.
Example 3: man, 45, 6 ft, 200 lb, light activity. 200 lb = 90.7 kg and 6 ft = 182.9 cm. BMR = 1,830 kcal/day; × 1.375 = 2,517 kcal/day to maintain weight.
Understanding your results
Maintenance calories (TDEE): an estimate of what keeps your weight stable. Track your weight for 2–4 weeks and adjust by about 100–200 kcal if it moves.
Equation choice: Mifflin-St Jeor is the default for most adults. Katch-McArdle can suit people who know their body-fat percentage, particularly if they are very lean or muscular.
Activity level is the biggest source of error. Most people overestimate their activity, so if in doubt, choose the lower level.
General reference values: the NHS says that, as a guide, an average man needs 2,500 kcal a day and an average woman 2,000 kcal. Your estimate may differ from these.
Safety: large deficits aren't appropriate for everyone. If you're pregnant, breastfeeding, under 18, have a medical condition, or have a history of eating disorders, ask a doctor or registered dietitian before changing what you eat.
Country notes
US: the Dietary Guidelines for Americans publish estimated calorie needs by age, sex and activity level.
UK: food labels show both kJ and kcal. Use the kJ toggle to compare directly.
Canada: nutrition labels use Calories (kcal). Health Canada's guidance focuses on food choices rather than calorie targets.
Tips and common mistakes
Overestimating activity. Choose the lower level if unsure.
Cutting calories too far. Large deficits can be hard to sustain and aren't suitable for everyone.
Ignoring the trend. Adjust after two to four weeks of weighing.
Counting exercise twice. Your activity level already includes it.
Frequently asked questions
How many calories should I eat a day?
It depends on your size, age, sex and activity. The calculator's maintenance figure is a personalised starting estimate. Population guides, such as the NHS's 2,000 kcal for women and 2,500 kcal for men, are averages.
What's the difference between BMR and TDEE?
BMR is the energy used at complete rest. TDEE adds the energy for daily movement and exercise. See the BMR calculator for more detail.
Which formula is most accurate?
None is exact for every individual. Mifflin-St Jeor is widely used for healthy adults. If you know your lean body mass, Katch-McArdle is an alternative. Real-world tracking beats any formula.
How quickly will I lose weight with a 500 kcal deficit?
It varies. Early loss is often faster (partly water), then slows as your body adapts and your weight drops. Use the NIH Body Weight Planner for a dynamic estimate.
Should I eat back calories burned in exercise?
If you chose an activity level that already includes your exercise, no. Adding exercise calories on top would count them twice.
Can I use this if I'm pregnant?
Energy needs change during pregnancy and breastfeeding. Ask your midwife, doctor or dietitian rather than relying on this calculator.

Calorie Deficit Calculator: Weight Loss by Date | FigSumo (57 chars)

H1: Calorie Deficit Calculator
A calorie deficit means eating fewer calories than your body uses, so it draws on stored energy, mostly fat. This calculator estimates your total daily energy expenditure (TDEE), then works out a daily calorie target for the rate of weight loss you choose and roughly how long it would take to reach a goal weight. It also flags targets that are lower than generally advised without medical supervision.
How to use this calculator
1. Units: metric or imperial.
2. Age, sex, height and current weight.
3. Activity level: sedentary to very active.
4. Goal weight.
5. Rate of loss: 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 or 1 kg a week (about 0.5, 1, 1.5 or 2 lb).
Results:
TDEE (maintenance calories)
Daily deficit for your chosen rate
Daily calorie target
Estimated weeks to goal and a goal date
A warning if the target falls below about 1,200 kcal (women) or 1,500 kcal (men), or the deficit exceeds 1,000 kcal a day
How it works
Step 1: BMR with the Mifflin-St Jeor equation:
Men:   10 × kg + 6.25 × cm − 5 × age + 5
Women: 10 × kg + 6.25 × cm − 5 × age − 161
Step 2: TDEE = BMR × activity factor (1.2, 1.375, 1.55, 1.725 or 1.9).
Step 3: daily deficit
Daily deficit = weekly loss (kg) × 7,700 ÷ 7
Target        = TDEE − daily deficit
Weeks to goal = (current weight − goal weight) ÷ weekly loss
7,700 kcal per kg (about 3,500 kcal per lb) is a long-standing rule of thumb for the energy in body fat. A 0.5 kg-a-week rate needs 550 kcal a day; 1 lb a week needs about 500 kcal a day.
Worked examples
Example 1: woman, 35, 80 kg, 165 cm, light activity, goal 70 kg
BMR = 800 + 1,031.25 − 175 − 161 = 1,495 kcal
TDEE = 1,495.25 × 1.375 = 2,056 kcal

Understanding your results
Weight loss slows over time. As you lose weight, your TDEE falls, and your body adapts. The 7,700 kcal rule doesn't account for this, so the "weeks to goal" figure is an optimistic minimum. The NIH Body Weight Planner uses a dynamic model that's more realistic for long periods.
Early losses are faster. The first week or two often includes water and glycogen, so the scale may drop faster at first.
Daily weights fluctuate by 1–2 kg. Use a weekly average.
Adjust after three to four weeks. If you're losing more slowly than planned, reduce intake by 100–200 kcal or increase activity.
How fast should you lose weight?
The NHS suggests aiming to lose 0.5 to 1 kg (1 to 2 lb) a week.
The CDC says people who lose weight gradually and steadily (about 1 to 2 lb a week) are more successful at keeping it off.
For many people with excess weight, losing 5% to 10% of body weight brings health benefits; for an 80 kg person that's 4–8 kg.
Very low-calorie diets (800 kcal a day or less) should only be followed with medical supervision.
Making a deficit work
Protein: around 1.2–1.6 g per kg helps preserve muscle and keeps you full. See the protein calculator.
Strength training two or more days a week helps keep muscle as you lose fat.
Fibre and volume: vegetables, fruit, legumes and whole grains add fullness for few calories.
Drinks: sugary drinks and alcohol are easy calories to cut.
Sleep: short sleep is linked with increased appetite.
Country notes
US: the CDC and the NIDDK Body Weight Planner are the main public resources.
UK: the NHS Weight Loss Plan is a free 12-week programme; the NHS uses the 0.5 to 1 kg a week guideline.
Canada: Obesity Canada's clinical practice guideline focuses on health improvements rather than a target weight.
Tips and common mistakes
Overestimating activity, which inflates TDEE and makes the target too high.
Underestimating food intake. Weighing food for a week or two helps calibrate.
Cutting too hard. Large deficits are harder to sustain and increase muscle loss.
Not recalculating after losing 5 kg or more.
Frequently asked questions
How big should my calorie deficit be?
For most people, 300 to 500 kcal a day, and rarely more than 1,000 kcal a day.
How many calories should I eat to lose 1 kg a week?
About 1,100 kcal a day below your TDEE, which may be too low for many people.
Is 1,200 calories a day safe?
It's often used as a lower limit for women without supervision, but needs vary; talk to a doctor or dietitian.
Why did my weight loss stop?
Your TDEE falls as you lose weight, and intake tends to creep up. Recalculate and review portions.
Do I need to count calories?
Not necessarily; any approach that creates a consistent deficit works.
Does exercise matter if I'm in a deficit?
Yes; it helps preserve muscle and improves health even when weight doesn't change.
Can I target belly fat?
No. Fat loss happens across the body, though waist size often falls as you lose weight.

Calories Burned Calculator by Activity (METs) | FigSumo (55 chars)

H1: Calories Burned Calculator
How many calories does an activity burn? This calculator estimates energy used during exercise or everyday activity from its MET value, your body weight and how long you do it. METs (metabolic equivalents) are a standard way of expressing how hard an activity is compared with sitting quietly.
How to use this calculator
1. Units and body weight.
2. Activity MET value: 1 MET is roughly the energy you use at rest. Look up the activity's MET in the table below or the Compendium of Physical Activities.
3. Duration (minutes).
Results: calories burned (estimate) in kcal, and the formula used.
The formula
Calories (kcal) = MET × Weight (kg) × Time (hours)
One MET is defined as about 1 kcal per kilogram of body weight per hour (equivalent to 3.5 ml of oxygen per kg per minute). An activity of 8 METs uses about eight times the energy of resting.
The result is gross energy: it includes the calories you'd have burned anyway at rest. To estimate the extra calories from exercise alone, use (MET − 1) instead.
Typical MET values
Calories for a 70 kg person over 30 minutes:

MET values come from the Compendium of Physical Activities, which lists hundreds of activities. Your actual effort can be higher or lower than the listed intensity.
Worked examples
Example 1: 45-minute run at 8 METs, 70 kg
Calories = 8 × 70 × 0.75 = 420 kcal
Net of resting energy: 7 × 70 × 0.75 = 368 kcal
Example 2: 30-minute brisk walk, 180 lb
180 lb = 81.6 kg
Calories = 3.5 × 81.6 × 0.5 = 143 kcal
Walking 30 minutes, 5 days a week, at 70 kg burns about 612 kcal a week in total.
Example 3: a weekday cycling commute
A 75 kg rider commutes 25 minutes each way, five days a week, at a leisurely 6.8 METs:
Per ride: 6.8 × 75 × 25/60 = 212 kcal
Per week (10 rides): 2,125 kcal, or 1,812 kcal above resting energy use
That's 250 minutes of moderate to vigorous activity, which more than meets the 150-minute weekly guideline on its own.

How long does it take to burn off a snack?
A 250 kcal chocolate bar needs about 250 ÷ (3.5 × 70) × 60 = 61 minutes of walking for a 70 kg person, or 22 minutes of running at 6 mph. That comparison is one reason food choices usually matter more than exercise alone for weight control.
Understanding your results
Estimates, not measurements. METs are averages for adults; fitness, efficiency, terrain, temperature and technique change real energy use. Individual results can differ by 20% or more.
Heavier people burn more for the same activity because moving more mass takes more energy.
Wearables estimate from heart rate and movement and may disagree with MET-based estimates.
Weight management: exercise calories add to your daily energy expenditure. Use the TDEE calculator for total daily needs and the calorie deficit calculator to plan changes. Don't simply "eat back" every estimated exercise calorie; the estimate may be generous.
Physical activity guidelines
United States: adults should aim for at least 150 to 300 minutes a week of moderate-intensity activity, or 75 to 150 minutes of vigorous activity, plus muscle-strengthening activities on 2 or more days (Physical Activity Guidelines for Americans).
Canada: the 24-Hour Movement Guidelines recommend at least 150 minutes of moderate to vigorous aerobic activity a week, muscle strengthening twice a week, and limiting sedentary time.
United Kingdom: the Chief Medical Officers advise at least 150 minutes of moderate or 75 minutes of vigorous activity a week, with strength activities on at least 2 days.
Moderate activities are roughly 3 to 5.9 METs; vigorous activities are 6 METs or more.
Calories and kilojoules on labels
US and Canadian food labels show energy as "Calories", meaning kilocalories. UK labels show both kilojoules (kJ) and kilocalories (kcal), with kJ first. To compare a UK label with this calculator, divide kJ by 4.184: a 1,757 kJ meal is about 420 kcal, the same as Example 1's run.
Tips and common mistakes
Counting the whole gym session when half was rest between sets.
Using a vigorous MET for a moderate effort.
Forgetting to convert pounds to kilograms (the calculator handles this when imperial units are selected).
Double-counting resting calories already in your TDEE.
Frequently asked questions
How are calories burned calculated?
By multiplying the activity's MET value by your weight in kg and the time in hours.
What is a MET?
A metabolic equivalent: the energy cost of an activity as a multiple of resting energy use.
How many calories does walking burn?
At 3 mph (about 3.5 METs), a 70 kg person burns about 120 kcal in 30 minutes.
Does a heavier person burn more calories?
Yes, for the same activity and duration.
Are fitness tracker calories accurate?
They're estimates too, and studies find wide errors for energy expenditure.
Should I eat back exercise calories?
It depends on your goals; many people eat back only part of the estimate.

Carbohydrate Calculator: Daily Carbs in Grams | FigSumo (55 chars)
Meta description
Turn your daily calories into a carbohydrate range in grams using the 45-65% of energy range from the Dietary Guidelines for Americans. (135 chars)

H1: Carb Calculator
Carbohydrates are the body's main fuel, particularly for the brain and for hard exercise. How much you need depends on your total energy needs, how active you are and your goals. This calculator estimates a daily carbohydrate target either as a share of your daily calories or in grams per kilogram of body weight, the method sports dietitians use.
How to use this calculator
1. Method: choose % of calories from carbs or grams per kg of body weight.
2. For the percentage method: enter daily calories (from the TDEE calculator or calorie calculator) and the carbohydrate %. The default is 45%.
3. For the g/kg method: enter body weight and carbs (g per kg). The default is 3 g/kg.
Results: daily carbohydrates in grams and the matching calories or share of calories.
The formulas
% method:   Carbs (g) = Daily calories × Carb % ÷ 4
g/kg method: Carbs (g) = Body weight (kg) × g per kg
Calories from carbs = Carbs (g) × 4
Carbohydrate provides about 4 kcal per gram.
Guideline ranges
General adults: the US Acceptable Macronutrient Distribution Range (AMDR) is 45% to 65% of calories from carbohydrate. The RDA is 130 g a day, the average minimum the brain uses.
Added sugars: less than 10% of calories (US Dietary Guidelines; UK free sugars limit is 5% of energy).
Fibre: 14 g per 1,000 kcal in the US guidelines (about 25 to 34 g a day for adults); the UK recommends 30 g a day.
Athletes (sports nutrition position statements): about 3 to 5 g/kg for moderate exercise of about an hour a day, 5 to 7 g/kg for moderate-to-high intensity training of 1 to 3 hours, and 6 to 10 g/kg or more for very high volumes [VERIFY current ranges].
Worked examples
Example 1: 2,000 kcal a day
45%: 2,000 × 0.45 ÷ 4 = 225 g
55%: 275 g
65%: 325 g
Fibre target: about 28 g. Keep added sugars under about 50 g.
Example 2: endurance training, 65 kg
At 5 g/kg: 325 g of carbohydrate a day (1,300 kcal). If total intake is 2,600 kcal, that's 50% of calories, within the general range.
Example 3: imperial units
150 lb (68.0 kg) at 3 g/kg → 204 g a day.
Example 4: heavy training, 70 kg
At 7 g/kg: 70 × 7 = 490 g a day (1,960 kcal). On a 3,200 kcal intake, that's 61% of calories, toward the top of the general range, which is normal for endurance athletes in heavy training.

Understanding your results
Quality matters as much as quantity. Whole grains, legumes, fruit, vegetables and dairy provide fibre, vitamins and minerals; refined grains and sugary drinks don't.
Low-carbohydrate diets (often under 26% of calories, or under 130 g) can work for weight loss or blood glucose for some people. At 1,800 kcal, 20% of calories is about 90 g. Discuss very low-carb plans with a clinician, particularly if you take diabetes medicines.
Diabetes: carbohydrate counting is used to match insulin doses; targets should be set with your diabetes care team.
Timing: for training, carbohydrate before and after sessions supports performance and recovery.
Country notes
United States: AMDR 45–65%; Nutrition Facts labels list total carbohydrate, fibre, total sugars and added sugars.
Canada: Health Canada uses the same Dietary Reference Intakes; Canada's food guide emphasises whole grains and vegetables, and labels show % Daily Value for fibre and sugars.
United Kingdom: the NHS recommends starchy foods make up just over a third of what you eat and that carbohydrate provides about 50% of energy; front-of-pack traffic-light labels flag high sugar.
Tips and common mistakes
Using grams of food instead of grams of carbohydrate. 100 g of cooked rice contains about 28 to 30 g of carbohydrate.
Forgetting carbohydrate in drinks such as juice, smoothies and sports drinks.
Choosing a percentage that doesn't fit protein and fat needs. Check the full split with the macro calculator.
Not adjusting on rest days if you train hard.
Frequently asked questions
How many carbs should I eat a day?
For most adults, 45% to 65% of calories, which is about 225 to 325 g on 2,000 kcal.
What is the minimum carbohydrate intake?
The RDA is 130 g a day for adults, based on the brain's glucose use.
How many grams of carbs per kg for athletes?
Roughly 3 to 10 g/kg depending on training volume and intensity.
How many calories are in a gram of carbohydrate?
About 4 kcal.
Do fibre grams count as carbs?
Fibre is a carbohydrate on labels, but it provides fewer usable calories. Some people count "net carbs" (total minus fibre).
Is a low-carb diet healthy?
It can be for some people in the short term; long-term effects depend on what replaces the carbohydrate.

Conception Date Calculator from Due Date or LMP | FigSumo (57 chars)
Meta description
Estimate the likely conception window from your last period, cycle length or due date. An estimate only; it cannot pinpoint a date. (131 chars)
Country
global

1,102 (minimum 1,000)
H1: Conception Date Calculator
Conception happens when sperm fertilises an egg, usually within a day of ovulation. Because ovulation dates vary and sperm can survive for several days, no calculator can pinpoint the exact day, but you can estimate it from the first day of your last menstrual period (LMP) or from your due date. This calculator works in both directions.
How to use this calculator
1. Known date: choose Last menstrual period or Due date.
2. Enter the LMP date or the due date.
3. Cycle length: your usual cycle, 21–45 days (default 28).
Results:
LMP mode: estimated conception date and estimated due date
Due-date mode: estimated conception date and estimated LMP
How it works
Conception ≈ LMP + (cycle length − 14) days
Due date   = LMP + 280 days
LMP (from due date) = due date − 280 days
The 14 days is the average luteal phase (from ovulation to the next period). For a 28-day cycle, conception is estimated on day 14.
In the current tool, the due date is always LMP + 280 days, whatever cycle length you enter, while the conception date moves with cycle length. For cycles much longer or shorter than 28 days, your clinician may adjust the due date, usually after a dating scan.
Worked examples
Example 1: LMP 4 May 2026, 28-day cycle
Estimated conception: 18 May 2026
Due date: 8 February 2027
Most likely window for the sex that led to conception: about 13 May 2026 to 19 May 2026 (sperm survive up to five days)
Example 2: due date 14 February 2027, 28-day cycle
Estimated LMP: 10 May 2026
Estimated conception: 24 May 2026
Example 3: LMP 4 May 2026, 32-day cycle
Conception: 22 May 2026, four days later than Example 1.
Many clinicians would also move the due date four days later, to 12 February 2027; the tool doesn't yet.
Understanding your results
It's an estimate. Even with regular cycles, ovulation can shift by several days.
Conception isn't necessarily the date of sex. Sperm can live up to five days, so conception can happen days after intercourse.
Dating scans are more accurate. A first-trimester ultrasound is the best way to date a pregnancy; it can move the estimated conception date too.
IVF: conception is known precisely from the embryo transfer and embryo age, so this calculator isn't needed.
Paternity questions: a calendar estimate can't establish paternity reliably when possible dates are close together. Only DNA testing can.

When to take a pregnancy test
Home tests detect hCG, a hormone produced after the embryo implants, usually 6 to 12 days after ovulation. For the 28-day cycle in Example 1, the next period would be due on 1 June 2026, and a test from that day is far more reliable than an early test. A negative result before a missed period doesn't rule out pregnancy; test again a few days later if your period hasn't started.
Pregnancy age vs fetal age
Pregnancy is counted from LMP (gestational age). Fetal age (from conception) is about two weeks less. At the due date, gestational age is 40 weeks and fetal age about 38 weeks.
Country notes
Dating conventions are the same in the US, Canada and the UK: all count from LMP and confirm with ultrasound. In the UK, the NHS dating scan is at 10–14 weeks; in the US and Canada, first-trimester ultrasound is commonly offered.
Tips and common mistakes
Using the last day of the period. Use the first day of bleeding.
Assuming conception was on the date of sex.
Ignoring your scan date. If your care team gave you a due date from a scan, use due-date mode.
Planning a pregnancy: advice by country
Folic acid: the NHS, the US CDC and Health Canada all advise 400 micrograms (0.4 mg) of folic acid a day for anyone who could become pregnant, ideally starting before conception and continuing through early pregnancy. Some people are advised a higher dose by their doctor.
When to ask for help, US: ACOG suggests an evaluation if you haven't conceived after 12 months of trying when under 35, after 6 months at 35 or over, and sooner over 40.
When to ask for help, UK: NICE advises seeing a GP if you haven't conceived after a year of regular unprotected sex, or earlier if you're 36 or over or have a known fertility issue.
When to ask for help, Canada: Canadian guidance follows the same 12-month and 6-month (age 35+) pattern [VERIFY against current SOGC guidance].
Cycle tracking is a sensible first step, but it doesn't replace a check-up if you have very irregular cycles, painful periods or a known condition.
Frequently asked questions
How do I work out when I conceived?
Add your cycle length minus 14 days to the first day of your last period.
Can I find the conception date from my due date?
Yes: subtract 280 days to get your LMP, then add cycle length minus 14.
How accurate is a conception date calculator?
It's usually within a few days, but not exact.
Can I get pregnant from sex a week before ovulation?
Unlikely; sperm survive up to about five days.
Why is my pregnancy two weeks "older" than conception?
Pregnancy is dated from your last period, about two weeks before ovulation.
Does cycle length affect my due date?
It can; longer cycles often mean a later due date.

Title tag
Due Date Calculator: Estimate Your Baby's Due Date | FigSumo (60 chars)
Meta description
Estimate your due date from your last period (any cycle length), conception date or IVF transfer date, and see weeks pregnant today and key milestones. (151 chars)
Country
global (date format follows locale: MM/DD/YYYY US, DD/MM/YYYY UK/CA option)
Status
keep
Body words
1,104 (minimum 1,000)
H1: Due Date Calculator
This calculator gives an estimated due date (EDD) from the information you have: the first day of your last menstrual period (LMP), a known conception date, or an IVF embryo transfer date. It also shows how many weeks pregnant you are today and the dates of common milestones. A due date is an estimate. Your midwife or doctor may confirm or adjust it after an early ultrasound scan, and that scan date should then take priority.
How to use this calculator
1. Choose a method:
Last period (default): the first day of your last period, plus your usual cycle length (28 days if you're not sure).
Conception date: if you know it, for example from ovulation tracking.
IVF transfer: the transfer date and the embryo's age at transfer (day 3, 5 or 6).
Ultrasound: if a scan has given you a date, enter it to see your milestones.
2. Results: the estimated due date, your gestational age today (weeks + days), and a milestone timeline.
Dates you enter are processed in your browser and are not sent to our servers.
The formula
Pregnancy is conventionally counted from the first day of the LMP, and a typical estimate is 280 days (40 weeks) from that date:
EDD (LMP method)        = LMP + 280 days + (cycle length − 28 days)
EDD (conception method) = conception date + 266 days
EDD (IVF)               = transfer date + 266 days − embryo age in days
                          (day-5 embryo: + 261 days; day-3: + 263 days; day-6: + 260 days)
Gestational age today   = today − LMP (or the equivalent LMP for other methods), in weeks and days
The cycle adjustment assumes ovulation happens about 14 days before the next period. In a longer cycle, ovulation and conception are later, so the due date moves later by the same number of days.
Worked examples
Example 1: last period, 28-day cycle. LMP: 2 March 2026.
2 March 2026 + 280 days = 7 December 2026
Gestational age on 14 October 2026: 226 days = 32 weeks 2 days
Milestones: 12 weeks on 25 May 2026; 28 weeks on 14 September 2026; 37 weeks on 16 November 2026; 42 weeks on 21 December 2026
Example 2: other methods give consistent results.
Longer cycle: the same LMP with a 32-day cycle → 280 + 4 = 284 days → 11 December 2026
Conception date: 16 March 2026 + 266 days → 7 December 2026, matching Example 1, as you'd expect for conception on day 14 of a 28-day cycle
IVF: a day-5 embryo transferred on 20 March 2026 → 20 March + 261 days → 6 December 2026
Example 3: a dating scan changes the date. A scan on 28 May 2026 measures the baby at 12 weeks 0 days. The equivalent LMP is 28 May − 84 days = 5 March 2026, giving a due date of 10 December 2026. That's 3 days later than the LMP estimate in Example 1, a difference small enough that many clinicians would keep the LMP date [VERIFY the threshold your care team uses].
Naegele's rule by hand. Add 7 days to the LMP and count back 3 months: 2 March 2026 → 9 March → 9 December 2026. That's two days later than the 280-day count because months have different lengths.
Understanding your results
Estimated, not exact: the NHS notes that pregnancy normally lasts from 37 to 42 weeks from the first day of the last period. Most babies are born within that window, not on the due date itself.
Ultrasound dating: ACOG states that early ultrasound, in the first trimester, is the most accurate way to establish or confirm gestational age. If your scan date differs from the LMP estimate, your care team will tell you which date to use.
Irregular cycles: if your cycle length varies a lot, an LMP-based estimate is less reliable. A dating scan matters more.
Gestational age vs weeks since conception: gestational age counts from the LMP, about two weeks before conception. This is the standard convention, so "8 weeks pregnant" means about 6 weeks after conception.
Country notes
UK: the NHS offers a dating scan at around 12 weeks, which can more accurately estimate how far along you are.
US: ACOG Committee Opinion 700 sets out how clinicians estimate and document the due date. A pregnancy without an ultrasound that confirms or revises the date before 22 weeks is considered suboptimally dated.
Canada: follow your provincial prenatal care provider. Most offer an early dating ultrasound (VERIFY a Canadian source, e.g. SOGC, before publishing).
Date formats: US users see MM/DD/YYYY by default; UK and Canadian users can choose DD/MM/YYYY.
Tips and common mistakes
Using the last day of your period. Use the first day.
Ignoring a dating scan. Your care team's scan date takes priority.
Treating the due date as fixed. Most babies arrive within two weeks either side.
Using LMP dating after IVF. Use the transfer date and embryo age.
Frequently asked questions
How is the due date calculated?
Most commonly, by adding 280 days (40 weeks) to the first day of your last menstrual period, adjusted if your cycle is longer or shorter than 28 days.
How accurate is my due date?
It's an estimate. Pregnancy normally lasts 37 to 42 weeks, so birth within a few weeks either side is normal. An early ultrasound gives a more accurate dating than the LMP alone.
What if I don't know the date of my last period?
Use the conception date if you know it. Otherwise, your midwife or doctor can date the pregnancy by ultrasound.
Why does a longer cycle push the due date later?
Ovulation usually occurs about 14 days before the next period. With a 32-day cycle, that's around day 18 instead of day 14, so conception, and the due date, are about four days later.
How is the due date calculated after IVF?
From the transfer date and the embryo's age. A day-5 embryo is treated as if conception happened 5 days before transfer, so the due date is 261 days after the transfer.
Can my due date change?
Your care team may revise it once, typically after the first ultrasound, if the measurements differ enough from the LMP estimate. Later changes are uncommon.
Is this calculator a substitute for prenatal care?
No. If you think you're pregnant, contact your GP, midwife, doctor or local health service for care and advice.

eGFR Calculator
